Let me identify and repair the unsupported claims. Item 1 attributes the "August 24" hearing date to the Kathmandu Post, but that detail came from the FreePressJournal fetch. Item 2's "70 million litres deficit" is my arithmetic inference, not stated in the source. Item 3 overstates what the legal challenges concern.

[{"claim": "Google's $15 billion data centre in Visakhapatnam, India faces public interest litigation in Andhra Pradesh High Court filed by Jal Biradari over water-supply strain on a nearby reservoir.", "url": "https://kathmandupost.com/world/2026/08/06/google-s-15-billion-india-data-centre-project-battles-water-wildlife-concerns", "date": "2026-08-06", "quote_fragment": "the project will strain water availability by putting stress on a nearby reservoir"}, {"claim": "Visakhapatnam, the Indian city hosting the Google-Adani data centre, receives 410 million litres of water daily against a requirement of 480 million litres, with rationing common.", "url": "https://www.freepressjournal.in/india/googles-15-billion-andhra-pradesh-data-centre-project-faces-water-wildlife-concerns-amid-legal-challenges", "date": "2026-08-06", "quote_fragment": "receives 410 million litres of water daily against a requirement of 480 million litres"}, {"claim": "The Google-Adani India data centre site in Visakhapatnam is approximately 860 metres from Kambalakonda Wildlife Sanctuary, raising separate environmental concerns alongside the water litigation.", "url": "https://www.freepressjournal.in/india/googles-15-billion-andhra-pradesh-data-centre-project-faces-water-wildlife-concerns-amid-legal-challenges", "date": "2026-08-06", "quote_fragment": "approximately 860 metres from Kambalakonda Wildlife Sanctuary, home to leopards and pangolins"}]
